dedupe_keys.name: open source digital twin of a gas distribution network in southern italy

description: This case study builds a digital twin of a real gas distribution network in Southern Italy entirely with open-source tools, to support the energy transition of gas networks. Filippo Luca Alberto Munafò, Marco Beccali and co-authors published it in Energies in 2025. The workflow covers the full digital lifecycle: consumption data from smart meters and GIS mapping of the network, 3D modelling in FreeCAD and QGIS, and hourly simulation of network operation in GasNetSim, with Python scripts that clean and harmonise the data. The simulations compute pressures, flow rates and gas quality indicators such as the Wobbe index. The authors report that the twin reproduced real network behaviour and supported scenario analysis for injecting greener gases such as hydrogen or biomethane, and that data quality and availability were critical. Coverage: one distribution network in Southern Italy. Access: open-access journal article; network data belong to the operator and are not released. Licence and cost: the article is CC BY 4.0 and free. Caveats: a single network, and the operator data and exact location are not public, so the workflow is reusable but results are not reproducible directly. It demonstrates digital twin, network flow and capacity planning methods for gas pipelines. It is an application of the GasNetSim model catalogued here and relates to the collection of publicly available gas network datasets and models.
